places.name: Eureka Maiala Court Margate
places.rent: Not published. Rentals only: no entry or exit fees, just a refundable rental bond. Eureka says it sets its rents so people who rely on the Age Pension can afford them, and residents may be eligible for Rent Assistance. Electricity, phone and internet are extra.
places.pets: Not stated for Margate (one directory lists it as 'Pet Policy Not Specific'). Eureka's general FAQ: 'Most of our villages are pet friendly, but restrictions do apply. The Eureka Villages Pet Policy must be strictly adhered to. Please contact your village manager for more information.'
places.access: Lift: 'Covered walkways provide all-weather protection and our elevator allows easy access to the Community Room and your neighbours.' One-bedroom unfurnished units with ensuite; units have private balconies, so some are upstairs - ask for a ground-floor unit or one on the lift.
places.nearby: Public transport 20 m, doctor 380 m, post office 700 m, pharmacy 750 m, shopping centre 750 m, Centrelink 900 m, hospital 1 km, Margate beach about 500 m (Eureka page and village flyer).
places.why: The only seniors rental village I found on the Redcliffe Peninsula: 1-bedroom units, a lift, a bus stop at the gate and shops 750 m away, with pension-friendly rent and no buy-in. Rent is not published and the cat needs the manager's OK, so ask about both.

places.name: Solstice (BHC seniors apartments, Redcliffe)
places.rent: 82 homes for people aged 55 and over: 59 social and 23 affordable. Social units: BHC says its social rents are 'not income-based but set at levels designed to be affordable for most people receiving Centrelink benefits' and it counts Rent Assistance when checking affordability. Affordable units: 74.9% of market rent; income limit for a single adult $64,992 a year (June 2026).
places.pets: BHC: 'we understand the value of pets and support residents in having one where possible', but 'not all BHC properties are suitable for a pet'. You apply to keep a pet (form, or pets@bhcl.com.au) with proof of microchipping and desexing for a cat; BHC replies within 14 days.
places.access: New multi-storey apartment building (opened late 2025). All homes built to Gold or Platinum Livable Housing Design standards so residents with varying mobility can age in place; one bedroom plus a multi-purpose room and a private balcony. Lifts are not spelled out in the sources I read - confirm.
places.nearby: BHC: 'Located just moments from Redcliffe's foreshore, shops, and essential services.' Bus and GP not stated.
places.why: Brand-new over-55s apartments in Redcliffe built for ageing in place, from a landlord that allows pets where it can. The social units come only through the Queensland Housing Register (then a BHC application form); the 23 affordable units are advertised on realestate.com.au when one falls vacant, and BHC checks she can afford the rent on her income.

places.name: Bric Housing Redcliffe units (Portwood Street)
places.address: Portwood Street, Redcliffe (street number not published)
places.rent: Income-based rent (community housing). Tenants come only by referral from the Queensland Housing Register.
places.access: 18 one-bedroom units built to Gold and Platinum Liveable Housing standards, with 'wider hallways and doors to make them suitable for people with decreased mobility and people who use a wheelchair'. Number of storeys and lift not stated.
places.why: A small, new, accessible complex in Redcliffe built for seniors and people with disability, but Bric says it has no waitlist of its own and only houses people referred by the Department of Housing, and its pet policy is not published.

places.name: Coast2Bay Housing Group (community housing across Moreton Bay)
places.suburb: Moreton Bay, including the Redcliffe Peninsula and Deception Bay
places.address: Various properties; Moreton Bay office listed at 16 King Street, Caboolture QLD 4510 (council guide, 2022)
places.rent: Community housing: 'rent based on what you can afford' (income-based). Its affordable housing (capped at 75% of market, no more than 30% of household income) is mostly on the Sunshine Coast and Banya.
places.access: Varies by property (houses, townhouses and 1-4 bedroom units).
places.why: A large community-housing landlord in Moreton Bay including the Redcliffe Peninsula, but I found no seniors-only complex, and its community housing is only offered through Department of Housing referrals, so the Housing Register is the way in.

places.name: Seasons Kallangur (Seasons Flexi Lease)
places.rent: From $340 per week (Seasons Kallangur page). Bond is four weeks' rent; first lease is six months; Rent Assistance can be claimed if eligible. A 2021 news article said the model included a meal service (three meals a day for about $80 a week) - ask whether meals are included or compulsory now.
places.pets: 'Seasons Flexi communities are pet-friendly and allow one pet to reside per unit, on application. Please note pets are not permitted in the communal dining area.' FAQ: 'Yes. We welcome pet cats, dogs, birds or fish.'
places.access: One-bedroom apartments with private courtyards, an accessible bathroom and flat garden paths in a gated community; Seasons' own site summary calls them ground level - confirm on a visit.
places.nearby: 'Located on Anzac Avenue, Seasons Kallangur is close to shops, sport clubs and medical services.' Bus not stated.
places.why: Seniors rental with one-bedroom apartments from $340 a week, a written pet policy that includes cats, no buy-in, and Seasons Home Care on site. It is full right now ('all our Rental Communities are currently at capacity'), so the step is to join the waitlist, which is offered first come, first served.

places.name: Kurrajong Townhouses
places.address: Kallangur QLD 4503 (street not published on the page)
places.rent: Affordable living at discounted market rent; 'Income to rent affordability must be within 30%'; assets under $141,500 for a single person. You apply directly for vacancies advertised on real estate websites.
places.pets: Not stated; the application steps include a 'Pet Application (if applicable)'.
places.access: 50 homes: 7 one-bedroom single-storey townhouses; the 2- and 3-bedroom townhouses are two storey.
places.nearby: Not stated; large community centre on site.
places.why: One of the few affordable rentals you can apply for directly, with seven single-storey one-bedroom homes, but it is a mixed family complex (not for seniors) and the rent must be no more than 30% of income, which is hard to meet on the pension alone.

places.name: Eureka Deagon (also listed as Oxford Crest Deagon Village)
places.rent: Not published ('Contact Us For Pricing & Availablities'). Rentals only, no buy-in, just a refundable bond; Eureka says it sets rents so Age Pension recipients can afford them, and residents may get Rent Assistance. Electricity, phone and internet are extra.
places.pets: 'Pet friendly' (Eureka Deagon page); the Downsizing listing says 'Pets Allowed'.
places.access: 'Single-level villa living' (Downsizing listing); self-contained 1-bedroom units with front and back doors, a verandah sitting area, split-system air-conditioning and an emergency call button.
places.nearby: 'Well-serviced by local buses and the Deagon train station (on the Shorncliffe line)'; close to Sandgate's shops, 'excellent doctor's practices, and pharmacies'.
places.why: Pension-friendly seniors rental with single-level 1-bedroom villas and a stated pet-friendly policy, near Sandgate's shops, buses and the train. It is in her third-choice area, and the rent has to be asked for.

places.name: Kedron Wavell Terraces (SunnyCove Retirement Village Chermside)
places.operator: Private operator, advertised as SunnyCove Retirement Village Chermside
places.rent: Not published ('Contact Agent'); the listing mentions 'Centrelink rent assistance eligibility'.
places.access: 44 units over two levels with 'lift access to upper units'; 1-bedroom units with ensuite and an individual courtyard.
places.nearby: Listing: 'walk-in only 1min to BUS STATION; 2min to LIBRARY; 2min to RSL CLUB; 5min to WESTFIELD'; doctors nearby and a short drive to hospital; meals cooked on site, visiting hairdresser and a courtesy bus to the RSL.
places.why: Over-50s rentals with a lift, right beside Westfield Chermside and the bus station, but it is in her last-choice area, has no website of its own, and rent and pet rules are not published (the ad is undated, so check it is current).

places.name: Carseldine Gardens
places.operator: Liberty Senior Living (on-site management; units privately owned)
places.rent: Not published. Units are rented out by their owners; a 2-bedroom there was advertised at $420 a week (bond $1,680) in August 2023, so a 1-bedroom villa may come in under that.
places.pets: Not stated for the village; one 2023 unit listing showed pets allowed.
places.access: One- and two-bedroom villas; which ones are single level is not stated.
places.nearby: Directory lists 'Walk to Shops', 'Access to local public transport' and a village bus.
places.why: A seniors village of 143 homes where you can rent rather than buy, with a manager, hair salon and village bus, but units come up one at a time through private landlords and the operator's own website no longer loads, so details need a phone call.

places.name: Dianella Apartments
places.address: Mitchelton QLD (street not published on the page)
places.rent: Community housing: 'a small amount of rent, based on your household income and Commonwealth Rent Assistance, where applicable.'
places.access: 49 'universally designed community housing apartments for seniors' (31 one-bedroom) over three levels with lift access; mobility-scooter charging bays.
places.why: Purpose-built seniors community housing with a lift, but it is in Brisbane's north-west, outside her listed suburbs, and the only way in is a Department of Housing referral from the Housing Register.

housingRegister: Call 13 QGOV (13 74 68), or the Moreton Bay Housing Service Centre in Caboolture on (07) 5432 0700 (moretonbayhsc@hpw.qld.gov.au), to apply by phone or book an appointment to join the Queensland Housing Register, which is how you get offered public 'seniors' units' for over-55s and community housing such as Solstice, Bric, Coast2Bay and Dianella (source: https://www.qld.gov.au/housing/public-community-housing/eligibility-applying-for-housing/guide-to-applying-for-housing-assistance/apply-for-housing and https://www.qld.gov.au/housing/public-community-housing/housing-service-centre).
